title: Traffic echoing pipeline: tenant brakes, sampling shims, cost-safe duplication
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Background: We need a low-risk way to run non-production model variants (canaries/A/B/shadow) against live traffic for behavioral validation without compromising tenant budgets or production SLOs. Goal: build a traffic-echoing pipeline that duplicates requests into a side-path, applies tenant-aware brakes (credit windows and soft throttles), supports adaptive sampling shims, ensures data isolation for PII-sensitive tenants, and exposes cost + quality telemetry for safe rollouts and automatic rollback triggers. Scope: API-gateway replication hook, streaming duplicator service, tenant credit controller, sample selector with workload heuristics, KV/response-sideband tagging, billing telemetry hooks, canary gating rules and auto-rollback signal plumbing. Out of scope for this ticket: UI for rollout control (Console work item tracked separately), long-term billing reconciliation (accounting team), and on-prem installer packaging. Acceptance criteria: 1) End-to-end request duplication for text-generation endpoints with <5ms median added latency to the primary path; 2) Configurable tenant credit windows that block duplication when tenant spend quota exceeded; 3) Sampling shims that adapt sampling rate based on model length distribution and recent cost burn; 4) Per-tenant isolation so duplicated requests never reach shared logging where PII could leak; 5) Production dashboards exposing duplicates-per-minute, cost-per-dup, quality deltas (BLEU/ROUGE/proxy metric), and an auto-rollback hook that flips the canary off when quality regression or cost spike thresholds are breached.
design_decisions: use-async-fire-and-tap model for duplication to avoid blocking main path
implement tenant credit controller as a central stateful service with local caches for fast checks
tag duplicates with opaque sideband metadata instead of changing request body to prevent model behavior differences
implementation_notes: Prototype will live under services/echo-duplicator. Start with a feature-flagged gateway hook that forwards a copy over gRPC to the duplicator. Duplicator will consult local LRU cache of tenant credits and a lightweight sampling policy engine. Responses from duplicates are stored to a sideband results bucket with strict access controls. We will instrument a separate cost-meter endpoint to emit per-duplicate estimated token cost into metrics pipeline (Prometheus->Loki/Tempo dashboards).
rollout_plan: 1) Deploy duplicator to canary fleet with gateway flag off; 2) Enable duplication for internal test tenants at 100% to validate correctness; 3) Enable for 1% of production traffic for a controlled non-sensitive tenant cohort with tenant-brakes enabled; 4) Ramp to 5%/10% while monitoring cost and quality dashboards; 5) Gate full production use behind billing safety window and QA sign-off. Auto-rollback: if quality regression >5% on proxy metric OR duplicate cost burn exceeds 120% of baseline projection for 5m, circuit trips and pipeline disabled for affected tenant cohort.
testing_plan: Unit tests for sampling engine and tenant-credit logic, integration test harness that replays production traces at reduced scale, chaos test that kills duplicator instances to validate graceful fail-open behavior (primary path must never be impacted), and a canary run against synthetic workload to validate billing telemetry correctness.
security_considerations: Duplicated payloads must be redacted where tenant settings request PII masking. Sideband storage uses tenant-scoped buckets with enforced KMS encryption and RBAC restricting access to research/QA engineers. Audit events emitted for each duplication action. Security review required before enabling for regulated tenants.

open_questions: Should we expose tenant credit window config to customers in Console or keep it strictly managed by infra?
What heuristic should sampling shim use for multi-turn chats where token distribution varies dramatically? Suggest experimenting with seq-length histogram based sampling.
Do we need a soft-penalty mode that reduces sample rate instead of full stop when credit drains?

implement tenant credit controller MVP and local cache eviction policy
complete integration tests and run replay against subset of production traces
